messages:
cora: quick q — merged the module split (module-db -> module-db-core + module-db-helpers). did we break provider constraints? the new modules reference hashicorp/postgres ~>1.5 but the root providers.lock still has 1.4 pinned. anyone run a full plan against staging?
miguel: saw the PR, ran a local init+plan. provider resolution wants 1.6. terraform complained about a mismatch with providers.lock. recommend regenerating the lock or pinning module-level required_providers.
raj: agree with miguel — prefer explicit required_providers in each module to avoid hoisting surprises. e.g.:
```
terraform {
  required_providers {
    postgres = {
      source  = "hashicorp/postgres"
      version = "~> 1.5"
    }
  }
}
```
miguel: exact. then run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` in CI to update providers.lock and commit. also confirm no provider_alias changes in the new modules.
dina: also FYI the helm chart update renamed the secret key: `db_password` -> `database_password`. if charts aren't updated pods will fail mount/render and crashloop.
cora: thanks — do we need a terraform state mv for provider alias changes or is it only plan-time?
raj: alias changes become a state issue only if resources were created with an aliased provider. check `terraform state list | grep postgres` and `terraform state show <resource>` for the provider attribute. if it references an aliased provider path you will need `terraform state mv` to point to the new provider instance.
ops-oncall: ran a quick smoke on staging: plan shows one resource that might require a state move (aws_db_instance.db) because the provider address changed after the refactor. i can handle the mv after lunch, but will need approval and a brief downtime window.
terraform-bot: CI: terraform plan (staging) finished — status: succeeded with warnings. Warning: provider version mismatch; providers.lock needs update. Artifacts: s3://redwood-terraform-reports/1797654321/plan.txt
cora: ok i'll open a tiny follow-up PR: add required_providers to the two new modules, update the secret key in the helm values and chart, and regenerate the providers.lock. can someone review when i send? cc @miguel @dina
miguel: i'll review in ~30m. if you include the exact `terraform providers lock` command and the CI artifact path it's faster.
dina: and please add a short note in the release notes about the secret key rename and the namespace where it lives so SRE can watch for crashes.
raj: one more heads-up — bumping postgres provider may change resource schema for `postgresql_role` attrs. run `terraform plan` with `-refresh=false` first to see what will change, then a dry-run apply in a dev cluster.
cora: got it. i'll include a checklist in the PR description: 1) add required_providers, 2) regen providers.lock, 3) update helm secret key, 4) smoke plan in staging, 5) state mv if needed, 6) canary deploy. will tag ops for the maintenance window. :thumbsup:
miguel: sounds good.
dina: one tiny suggestion — add a redeploy annotation to the deployment to force a rolling restart after secret rename, e.g. `kubectl patch deploy -n prod svc --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood.com/redeploy":"$(date +%s)"}}}}}'`
cora: lol thanks raj + dina + miguel. sending PR now.
